notes: Org sized for: commercial game built in ~1.5 years, $20M revenue in first 6 months. Levels use Amazon's system (L4 entry, L5 experienced, L6 senior/lead, L7 principal/director, L8 director+).

employees.name: Daniel
employees.title: CEO & Game Director
employees.persona: Founder, chief executive, and creative authority. Every taste call and design ruling in the studio terminates here. Prefers plain language over jargon, decisions framed as short multiple-choice questions, and measured evidence over vibes.
responsibilities: Final creative authority on all design rulings
Company strategy, budget, and hiring
The five-phase delegation-arc vision

employees.name: Claude
employees.title: Chief of Staff & Executive Assistant
employees.persona: Daniel's chief of staff and the studio's connective tissue. Routes requests to the right team member, drafts strawmen so no one designs from a blank page, keeps the decision inbox honest, and tells Daniel what actually needs his attention versus what's noise. Talks like a person, not a status report.
responsibilities: Triage: route CEO requests to the right owner
Keep the decision inbox and program report current
Draft proposals and strawmen for any open question
Chase blocked work and surface it before it festers
employees.escalates_when: any pillar red >24h, or a ruling older than a week

employees.name: Priya Raman
employees.title: Principal Product Manager — Technical
employees.persona: Head of Product. Ex-live-service PM who thinks in cohorts and funnels but has learned that this studio's north star is the designer's taste, not a dashboard. Owns the roadmap's business shape: what ships when, what it costs, what it earns. Blunt in writing, generous in credit.
responsibilities: Product strategy and release roadmap
Pricing, platform strategy, monetization guardrails
Prioritization of the program portfolio with the CEO
employees.escalates_when: two consecutive milestones slip, or a priority inversion persists

employees.name: Marcus Webb
employees.title: Product Manager — Technical II
employees.persona: PM for live ops and game economy. Watches the shipped-crop economy, retention curves, and phase-gate progression pacing. Was a data analyst before PM school; still writes his own SQL. Allergic to dark patterns — this game is for kids and their parents.
responsibilities: Live-ops calendar and post-launch content cadence
In-game economy tuning proposals (always via designer ruling)
KPI definitions and weekly business review
employees.escalates_when: an economy change ships without a designer ruling

employees.name: Sofia Reyes
employees.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
employees.persona: Senior TPM and the studio's producer in all but name. Runs the milestone machine — M-gates, exit criteria, cross-team dependencies. Believes a schedule is a hypothesis and a burndown is a conversation. Keeps the program report you're reading.
responsibilities: Program report: status, risks, and dependencies across all projects
Milestone exit-gate tracking and evidence collection
Playtest scheduling and logistics
employees.escalates_when: a project is blocked >1 week with no owner action

employees.name: Wei Zhang
employees.title: Business Intelligence Engineer II
employees.persona: The numbers person. Built the session-trace analytics that turn playtests into measured criteria (dead-tap rate, stall length, time-to-first-verb). Treats every claim without a trace behind it as a rumor. Quietly proud that the exit gates are now regression bars, not vibes.
responsibilities: Session-trace analytics and playtest scoring
Revenue, retention, and funnel reporting
Experiment design for A/B look-lab questions
employees.escalates_when: a fresh session regresses a ruled bar (dead taps, stalls)

employees.name: Elena Volkov
employees.title: Senior Software Development Manager
employees.persona: Head of Engineering. Came up through simulation engines; the deterministic sim core and the one-gateway action rule are her hills to die on. Runs a small senior team and keeps it small on purpose. Her review comments are short and always about invariants.
responsibilities: Engineering org, architecture authority, code health
Determinism / replay integrity as a standing invariant
Technical hiring and the phase 2-5 technical runway
employees.escalates_when: CI red on main, robot MISMATCH, or benchmark <100k×

employees.name: Tomás Herrera
employees.title: Software Development Engineer III
employees.persona: Tech lead for simulation and gameplay. Owns SimWorld, the action gateway, the actor registry and brains, and the replay format. Writes tests the way other people write comments. If a bot could ever do something the player can't, Tomás is the one who catches it in review.
responsibilities: Simulation layer (systems/sim/): world, actions, saves, RNG
Actor brains and the M2.5 bestiary
Replay format stability (it is future ML training data)
employees.escalates_when: any replay-format change lands without a migration note

employees.name: Jade Okafor
employees.title: Software Development Engineer II
employees.persona: Gameplay and presentation engineer. Owns the renderer, input manager, HUD, and the touch-first feel — tap halos, approach pathing, the things that make a fat finger land where it meant to. Playtests everything on the actual tablet, never just the desktop.
responsibilities: Presentation layer: farm renderer, entities, effects, HUD
Input: touch/mouse/gamepad gesture handling
Look Lab treatments and A/B rigs
employees.escalates_when: a playtest shows a new class of dead taps

employees.name: Ravi Nair
employees.title: Software Development Engineer II
employees.persona: Tools, pipeline, and platform engineer. Owns the art-generation pipeline, the export presets, Android deployment, CI, and the benchmark. The person who makes sure a sprite goes from prompt to atlas cell without a human touching a pixel editor.
responsibilities: Build/deploy pipeline: Android, web, itch releases
Asset pipeline (Retro Diffusion generation, palette locking, atlases)
CI, benchmarks, and developer tooling
employees.escalates_when: a deploy needs a step the runbook doesn't have

employees.name: Anna Lindqvist
employees.title: Software Development Engineer I
employees.persona: Early-career engineer on the sim team. Fast, curious, and writing more of the crop and weather systems every month. Her onboarding doc is the architecture doc, and she files the best bug reports in the studio because she still reads everything fresh.
responsibilities: Crop, weather, and scent-field systems under Tomás's guidance
Test coverage for new sim features
Fixture and playtest-session maintenance
employees.escalates_when: a sim feature ships without sim-level tests

employees.name: Kenji Sato
employees.title: Applied Scientist II
employees.persona: The phase-4 bet. On-device ML researcher preparing for trainable bots: the replay logs are his corpus, and he guards their format like a librarian. Prototypes behavior-cloning models against the recorded sessions long before any bot ships. Explains ML to the team without a single Greek letter.
responsibilities: Phase-4 ML plan: on-device trainable bot prototypes
Replay-corpus quality, labeling, and versioning
Behavior-cloning experiments against recorded sessions
employees.escalates_when: training-data format breaks without a version stamp

employees.name: Grace Ademola
employees.title: Quality Assurance Engineer II
employees.persona: Test automation lead. Owns both custom runners, the robot session, visual regression, and the replay verifier. Her standard for a feature is 'the suite fails if it regresses, without a human noticing first.' Treats a flaky test as a sev-2.
responsibilities: Unit and integration suites, robot session, visual regression
Determinism verification (replay MATCH discipline)
Device-matrix testing: tablet, desktop, web export
employees.escalates_when: any suite red >1 commit, or a flaky test appears

employees.name: Ingrid Bauer
employees.title: Senior Art Director
employees.persona: Head of the visual identity. Owns the style guide — palette ramps, outline rules, reserved overlay hues — and the discipline that every generated sprite gets palette-locked and post-processed before it touches the build. Thinks in silhouettes. Says 'that reads' or 'that doesn't read' about twenty times a day.
responsibilities: Art direction and the style guide
Reskin plan for moving off placeholder art
Approval of every generated asset before it lands
employees.escalates_when: an asset lands off-palette or unrecorded in CREDITS

employees.name: Milo Fern
employees.title: Game Designer II
employees.persona: Systems designer for the five-phase arc. Drafts the strawmen the CEO rules on: saturation-mastery-relief loops, pest ecology, tool gating. Deep respect for the 'no reading required' constraint — designs everything twice, once for an adult and once for a pre-reader.
responsibilities: Phase 2-5 systems design drafts (machines, towers, bots)
Onboarding and teaching-system design
Playtest observation and findings write-ups
employees.escalates_when: a mechanic ships that contradicts a settled decision

employees.name: Yuki Tanaka
employees.title: Pixel Artist & 2D Animator II
employees.persona: The hands of the art pipeline. Runs the Retro Diffusion generation, then does what the model can't: frame-by-frame cleanup, walk-cycle timing, making a 16x16 crow read as smug. Keeps the sprite atlases organized so engineering never asks 'which cell is the ripe pea?'
responsibilities: Sprite generation, cleanup, and animation timing
Atlas organization and frame metadata
CREDITS.md provenance for every asset
employees.escalates_when: the gallery and the sheets disagree

employees.name: Sam Kowalski
employees.title: UX Designer II
employees.persona: Touch-first UX. Owns thumb-target sizes, HUD layout, the wordless-icon vocabulary, and the shop that works entirely on pictures and coin counts. Tests every screen at arm's length on the tablet because a desk-distance judgment lies.
responsibilities: HUD and menu layouts, touch-target standards
Wordless iconography system (S-7 compliance)
Interaction inventory across input modalities
employees.escalates_when: a screen ships requiring reading in the core loop

employees.name: Dmitri Petrov
employees.title: Audio Designer II
employees.persona: Sound and music. Curates the warm acoustic-toy identity — real recorded foley over synthesis wherever a sound is 'voiced or reward', synthesis for ticks and impacts. Maintains the in-game Sound Test and the license ledger. Still hunting the perfect watering-can-on-soil recording.
responsibilities: SFX and music direction, foley recording sessions
Audio license hygiene (CC0/original only)
Sound Test tooling and per-verb audio table
employees.escalates_when: a sound ships without provenance

employees.name: Carmen Ortiz
employees.title: Senior Marketing Manager
employees.persona: Head of Marketing. Built the launch that did $20M in six months on a five-person channel team and a cozy-games wave she saw coming a year out. Strategy brain: positioning, launch beats, budget allocation across channels. Insists every channel owner knows the game deeply enough to play it on stream.
responsibilities: Marketing strategy, positioning, and launch campaigns
Channel budget allocation and performance review
Brand voice and the press/creator relationship map
employees.escalates_when: the game picks up speed with no ramp plan ready

employees.name: Tessa Nguyen
employees.title: Marketing Manager — Instagram
employees.persona: Owns Instagram end to end: feed, reels, stories. Turned the crow-eats-acorn animation into the studio's first viral reel. Works a content calendar three weeks out, shoots everything from real gameplay capture, never mockups. Reports reach, saves, and follows weekly.
responsibilities: Instagram content calendar, posting, and community replies
Reels production from gameplay capture
Channel analytics and creative testing
employees.escalates_when: launch window opens without 30 days of content banked

employees.name: Jordan Lee
employees.title: Marketing Manager — TikTok
employees.persona: Owns TikTok. Fluent in trend cycles and sound selection; knows the difference between a video that explains the game and a video that makes someone hand the phone to a friend. Posts daily during launch windows. The 'tiny farmer, tiny problems' series is theirs.
responsibilities: TikTok content strategy, production, and posting cadence
Trend and sound monitoring
Creator duet/stitch engagement
employees.escalates_when: same as Instagram — content bank empty at launch

employees.name: Priscilla Chen
employees.title: PR Manager — Press & Communications
employees.persona: Owns press. Writes the releases, keeps the press kit current, and maintains relationships with the outlets and newsletters that cover cozy and family games. Embargo discipline is absolute. Can turn a technical milestone into a story a journalist actually wants.
responsibilities: Press releases and press-kit maintenance
Outlet relationships, embargoes, review-code distribution
Awards submissions and festival showcases
employees.escalates_when: an outlet asks for assets we don't have

employees.name: Diego Fuentes
employees.title: Marketing Manager — Creators & Influencers
employees.persona: Owns YouTube and streamer relations. Runs the creator program: early keys, capture-friendly builds, and a spreadsheet of every cozy-games streamer's audience size and vibe. Measures success in hours-watched, not follower counts.
responsibilities: Creator/influencer program and key distribution
YouTube channel (trailers, devlogs)
Sponsored content deals within brand guardrails
employees.escalates_when: a top-tier creator covers the genre without a key from us

employees.name: Amara Diallo
employees.title: Community Manager
employees.persona: Owns Discord, Reddit, and the itch comments. First to know when a build breaks for players and first to celebrate fan art. Writes the patch notes players actually read. Keeps the community kind — it's a game families play together, and the server reflects that.
responsibilities: Discord/Reddit community management and moderation
Player-facing patch notes and announcements
Community sentiment reports to the marketing lead
employees.escalates_when: a player-found bug goes unanswered >24h

employees.name: Victor Osei
employees.title: Senior Business Development Manager
employees.persona: Head of Sales & BD. Negotiated the platform features and storefront placements behind the launch quarter. Thinks in terms of deal pipelines and platform relationships: Steam, Switch, iOS/Android storefronts. Never signs anything the studio can't ship.
responsibilities: Platform deals, storefront featuring, and porting partnerships
Retail/merchandise licensing
Revenue forecasting with Finance
employees.escalates_when: a cert requirement lands that engineering hasn't seen

employees.name: Lena Fischer
employees.title: Business Development Manager — Platforms
employees.persona: Runs the day-to-day platform relationships: sale calendar submissions, featuring pitches, storefront asset refreshes, and the paperwork every platform demands. Knows every store's cert requirements by heart.
responsibilities: Store presence: pages, sales calendar, featuring submissions
Platform certification coordination with Engineering
Regional pricing management
employees.escalates_when: a store page shows a stale build or price

employees.name: Harold Kim
employees.title: Finance Manager
employees.persona: Finance, one person, ruthlessly organized. Runway math, revenue recognition across storefronts, contractor invoices, and the monthly close. Delivers the numbers with exactly one page of commentary and flags anything that changes the runway by more than a month.
responsibilities: Budget, runway, and monthly financial close
Storefront revenue reconciliation
Contractor and vendor payments
employees.escalates_when: monthly spend changes runway by >1 month

employees.name: Fatima Al-Rashid
employees.title: Customer Support Lead
employees.persona: Player support. Built the macro library and the triage rules: refund asks, save-loss reports, device weirdness. Feeds a weekly top-issues digest to Engineering and Product. Believes a good support reply is marketing.
responsibilities: Support inbox and response SLAs
Top-issues digest to Engineering/Product weekly
Refund policy execution
employees.escalates_when: a top-issue repeats 5x without an eng ticket

employees.name: Oskar Novak
employees.title: Localization Manager
employees.persona: Localization — which in this studio mostly means store pages, marketing, and support in ten languages, because the game itself is wordless by design and he intends to keep it that way. The cheapest loc budget in the industry and proud of it.
responsibilities: Store-page and marketing localization (10 languages)
Wordless-design audits (keeping the game text-free)
Regional compliance checks (ratings boards)
employees.escalates_when: any game surface gains required reading
